To Read Bhaskar English… Better News Experience Read in App In the Browser Continue Ahead of Raksha Bandhan, Deputy Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary has announced several initiatives for women and girls in Bihar. The state government has pledged to connect 1 crore women with employment opportunities over the next three years. Loading advertisement... Under the ‘Bihar Ki Beti Startup Challenge’ scheme, women will receive financial assistance ranging from ₹50,000 to ₹2 lakh to launch new startups. The government will also deploy ‘Police Didi’ (Abhaya Brigade) teams to improve the safety of female students in schools and colleges. A total of 4,700 scooters and motorcycles will be provided for the initiative. Free bus travel for women on August 27 and 28 Loading advertisement... As a Raksha Bandhan gift, women will be able to travel free of charge on state transport buses from the morning of August 27 until 10pm on August 28 . Women will not have to pay any fare on more than 1,000 buses operated by the Bihar State Road Transport Corporation during this period. The initiative aims to make it easier for women to visit their maternal homes and meet family members during Raksha Bandhan. ‘Police Didi’ to receive 4,700 scooters and motorcycles A total of 4,700 scooters and motorcycles will be handed over to ‘Police Didi’ teams, with Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary scheduled to flag off the vehicles. Under the scheme, 1,000 female students will receive financial assistance of ₹10,000 per month for four years. The fellowship is aimed at supporting women pursuing higher education and research. The financial assistance will help recipients meet expenses related to their PhD studies, research and other associated requirements, while encouraging more female students to pursue advanced education and research. ‘Bihar Ki Beti Startup Challenge’ scheme The government will also launch the ‘Bihar Ki Beti Startup Challenge’ to promote entrepreneurship among women and girls in the state. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary launches 3 major schemes for women empowerment and safety
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary launches 3 major schemes for women empowerment and safety; 'Police Didi' initiative rolled out ANI | Updated: Aug 26, 2026 13:06 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna (Bihar) [India], August 26 (ANI): Highlighting the state government's thrust on security and self-reliance, Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Wednesday rolled out three major schemes aimed at women's empowerment and safety, asserting that women's participation from panchayats to administration reflects the changing face of society in Bihar. Under the newly launched 'Police Didi' campaign, female police personnel will be deployed across schools, colleges, and other educational institutions to ensure the safety and security of young girls and women. To enhance their mobility on field duty, around 2,700 scooties and more than 2,000 motorcycles are being provided to women personnel. Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary highlighted that around 40,000 women police personnel are currently serving in the state force. He also noted that the emergency response time for the 'Dial 112' helpline has dropped below 10 minutes, with the administration targeting to reduce it further to 5-7 minutes. Emphasising economic self-reliance, the Chief Minister stated that 1.81 crore women are associated with the JEEViKA initiative in Bihar, with over 70 lakh 'JEEViKA Didis' actively working. He pointed out that 43 lakh women have already become 'Lakhpati Didis', and an additional target has been set to elevate one lakh more women into the category over the next two years. The Chief Minister further stated that when women become financially self-reliant, the entire family grows economically stronger. He emphasised that women's safety, education, and self-reliance will become the hallmark of a new and prosperous Bihar. Referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's goal of a 'Viksit Bharat' (Developed India) by 2047, the Chief Minister said that women's active participation will further strengthen this vision. Citing the improved road network and connectivity in Bihar, the Chief Minister also referenced Sudha Murty's visit to the state, sharing that she praised Bihar's roads and travel infrastructure. Earlier on Tuesday, Choudhary announced the launch of the "Student Support Camp" initiative to ensure prompt resolution of students' complaints, problems and suggestions. In a post on X, the Chief Minister said the camps would be organised every month on the fourth Tuesday at educational institutions, allowing students to directly raise their concerns with the government and concerned officials. He said students would also be able to register their grievances online through the "Student Support Portal" and Helpline 1100 and track the status of their complaints. "Every student's voice heard, every problem resolved--this is the resolve, this is the effort," Choudhary said. The initiative aims to provide students with a direct platform to communicate their concerns to the government and ensure timely action on their grievances. Under the initiative, students will be able to raise issues directly at educational institutions during the monthly camps, while the online portal and helpline will provide additional channels for registering complaints and monitoring their status. (ANI)

bihar_raw_news.title: Crores pursue BA, BCom degrees with weak job links: NITI Aayog flags urgency of ... - Mint
bihar_raw_news.content: NITI Aayog flags urgency of reimagining higher education in India: 'Crores pursue BA, BCom degrees with weak job links' The report flags that many young people are earning conventional degrees but not necessarily the skills employers need and calls for greater industry participation and wider use of Public-Private Partnership (PPP) models to bridge the gap between education and employment. Gulam Jeelani Updated 26 Aug 2026, 08:00 AM IST Patna, Bihar, India -Aug.25, 2026: Police personnel using water canon on members of the All Bihar Students' Union as they take out a 'Lok Bhavan March' against the Bihar government, protesting issues such as paper leaks, unemployment, and alleged irregularities in the 70th BPSC examination, at Dak Bungalow crossing in Patna, Bihar, India, Tuesday,Aug,25, 2026.(Photo by Santosh Kumar/ Hindustan Times) AI Quick Read India’s higher education system faces a structural imbalance, with crores of students opting for generic undergraduate degrees that often have weak links to employment, a recent NITI Aayog report has flagged. This trend reflects a broader structural imbalance across degree colleges, Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) and polytechnics, and underlines the need to rethink India’s higher education and skilling ecosystem, the report said. Also Read | NTA must be scrapped or reformed? Experts answer critical question Citing Economic Survey 2024–25 , the report said that only 8.25 per cent of graduates are employed in roles aligned to their qualifications. Educated unemployment is also high, as 13 per cent of all graduates and 20.4 per cent of graduate women are unemployed, far above the national unemployment rate of 3.2 per cent, it noted. “Compounding this is the overwhelming inclination toward generic degree programmes with weak job linkages. Of the 3.4 crore students enrolled in undergraduate programmes, 1.13 crore are in B.A. alone, and combined enrolment in B.A., B.Sc., and B.Com exceeds 2 crore. Many pursue these degrees primarily to remain eligible for government job, with 1.86 crore applications for just 55,000 posts between November 2024 to July 2025,” the report titled ‘ Reimagining Skilling for Viksit Bhara t’ released last week said. View full Image the report titled ‘Reimagining Skilling for Viksit Bharat’ released last week said NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) is the apex public policy think tank of the Government of India. Key challenge for India’s workforce The report flags a key challenge for India’s workforce: many young people are earning conventional degrees but not necessarily the skills employers need. The report called for greater industry participation and wider use of Public-Private Partnership (PPP) models to bridge the gap between education and employment. Such partnerships, it said, could help modernise curricula, introduce more job-linked learning and ensure that skilling programmes remain aligned with changing industry requirements and actual employment opportunities. “This structural imbalance (across degree colleges, ITIs, and polytechnics) underscores the urgency of reimagining higher education through stronger industry participation and Public-Private Partnership (PPP) models, the report suggested. These partnerships are critical to modernising curricula, embedding job-linked learning, and ensuring that skilling remains current, relevant, and connected

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar : Patna protests intensify as Prashant Kishor backs students, farmers | MorungExpress
bihar_raw_news.content: (Photo: IANS) India 25th August 2026 Patna, August 25 (IANS) Patna witnessed a tense day on Tuesday as student organisations protesting recruitment and examination issues joined farmers opposing the proposed Pataliputra Greenfield Satellite Township in demonstrations across the city. Police erected barricades at several locations to prevent student protesters from marching towards Lok Bhavan. Reacting to the police action, Bankipur MLA Prashant Kishor said recent events had demonstrated the strength of democracy. He argued that authorities now appeared to think twice before using force against protesters, describing this as a positive development. Kishor urged the government to address what he termed the legitimate demands of students and farmers, saying such concerns could not simply be suppressed. He highlighted issues including alleged privatisation and commercialisation of education, the growing influence of coaching institutes, examination paper leaks, rising unemployment and dissatisfaction among youth. He warned that failing to address these concerns could lead to larger student movements in the future. When reporters told him student aspirants were looking for him, Kishor said he was already in Patna and regularly moving around the city. Alongside the student protests, farmers from Punpun, Naubatpur, Masaurhi, Fatuha and surrounding areas demonstrated against the township project. Kishor backed their concerns, alleging that the government’s land policy could benefit major industrialists at farmers' expense. He claimed valuable agricultural land could be transferred at inadequate prices, arguing that the policy was difficult to implement in Bihar and warning that attempts to acquire large areas of productive land could lead to widespread unrest. Farmers said their agricultural land was their primary source of livelihood and that they produced three crops a year. They argued that surrendering land would threaten their families’ ability to fund education, marriages and other essential expenses. Protesters demanded the government reconsider the proposed acquisition, maintaining they did not want to surrender their land. Patna District Magistrate, SSP and SP reached the protest site and held discussions with farmer representatives, attempting to persuade them to resolve the matter through dialogue. The Bihar government has proposed developing 12 townships across the state, including the Pataliputra Greenfield Satellite Township. Farmers opposing the Patna project insist their agricultural land should not be acquired for development.

national_raw_news.content: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today said that India stands as the fastest-growing major economy in the world and offers a unique combination of scale, sustained growth, a young population, expanding consumption and rapidly deepening capital markets. Addressing prominent members of the Indian business community in Toronto today, Sitharaman said India’s transformation is structural, driven by rapid urbanisation, a growing middle class and world-class digital infrastructure. She noted that these developments are creating new opportunities across virtually every sector of the economy. The Finance Minister also highlighted the role of India’s digital ecosystem in transforming access to financial and commercial services. She underlined significant opportunities for collaboration with Canadian banks, fintech companies and regulators, not only in payments but also in shaping the next generation of digital financial infrastructure. Highlighting the growing India-Canada economic partnership, Sitharaman said the Indian diaspora in Canada serves as a strategic bridge between the two countries. She said India-Canada bilateral ties have undergone a remarkable transformation in recent times, supported by shared democratic and pluralistic values, expanding economic engagement, high-level interactions and strong people-to-people ties. Referring to the agreement reached between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Canadian counterpart Mark Carney on the sidelines of the G7 Summit in June 2025 to reset bilateral ties, Sitharaman said the two countries have reaffirmed their commitment to building a future-focused strategic partnership. Union Minister Nirmala Sitharaman arrived in Toronto yesterday for a four-day official visit to Canada, focused on strengthening bilateral trade, investment linkages and financial cooperation.

national_raw_news.title: 20 mins ago | National 37 IMA issues public health advisory on H1N1 influenza spread in country; Says, no cause for panic j...
national_raw_news.content: The Indian Medical Association (IMA) has urged people to remain vigilant amid a seasonal rise in Influenza A (H1N1) cases, saying that the majority of infections are mild and self-limiting and there is no cause for panic. The IMA has advised people not to take antibiotics over the counter for flu symptoms, stressing that H1N1 is a viral infection and antibiotics do not kill viruses. It specifically cautioned against self-medication with antibiotics such as azithromycin, amoxicillin-clavulanate and cefixime. According to the association, antibiotics should be taken only when prescribed by a qualified medical professional. The IMA said H1N1 commonly presents with sudden onset of high-grade fever and chills, persistent dry cough, sore throat, severe muscle aches and fatigue. Other symptoms may include headache, runny or congested nose, nausea, vomiting and loose stools. The association has recommended basic preventive measures to reduce the spread of infection. These include frequent handwashing with soap and water for at least 20 seconds or using an alcohol-based hand sanitiser. People have also been advised to follow respiratory hygiene by covering their mouth and nose with a tissue or bent elbow while coughing or sneezing. Wearing a well-fitted mask in crowded and enclosed spaces has also been recommended.

national_raw_news.title: Festival of Onam being celebrated with traditional fervour 25 mins ago 161
national_raw_news.content: Keralites across the globe are celebrating Thiru Onam today. Akashvani correspondent reports that Thiru Onam celebrations began with Ona Pookkalam, the traditional floral carpet made to welcome the legendary King Mahabali. This harvest festival is celebrated by Keralites irrespective of caste and religion. Special poojas are being held at temples, including the hill shrine of Sabarimala, Aranmula and Guruvayur. Ona Sadya, the traditional Kerala feast, is another major attraction of Thiru Onam. Thousands of cultural programmes and traditional games will be held across Keralam this afternoon, including official celebrations. Heavy rush is being experienced at temples across the state, despite the rain. President Droupadi Murmu has extended greetings and best wishes to all citizens, especially the people of Keralam living in India and abroad. In her message, President Murmu noted that Onam is an occasion to express gratitude to nature on the arrival of the new harvest. She added that the festival celebrates India’s rich culture and spirit of brotherhood, promoting unity in diversity. The President mentioned that Boat races, folk dances, music and sports are important traditions associated with this festival, which showcase the culture and values of Keralam. President Murmu prayed that this auspicious festival brings happiness, peace, good health and prosperity to all and inspires the citizens to contribute to the nation’s progress. Vice President C P Radhakrishnan has extended greetings to everyone on the occasion of Onam. Sharing a social media post, the Vice President prayed that this cherished festival, which reflects Keralam’s rich cultural heritage and timeless traditions, fill every home with happiness, good health and prosperity. Mr Radhakrishnan wished that the spirit of Onam strengthen harmony, unity and hope in society. Prime Minister Narendra Modi also extended greetings to the countrymen on the occasion of Onam. Sharing a social media post, the Prime Minister said that the vibrant festival is celebrated all over the world with great enthusiasm. Mr Modi wished that this festival further empowers the spirit of happiness, togetherness, and prosperity. Home Minister Amit Shah has extended greetings to the people of Keralam on the occasion of Onam. Sharing a social media post, Mr Shah prayed that this joyous occasion usher in a year filled with peace, prosperity and well-being for all.

Sign In Prefer Prefer PM Modi (Pic Via PIB) Prime Minister Narendra Modi has raised doubts over the effectiveness of quality checks in government construction and infrastructure work, The Times of India reported . He asked senior officials, "Do we now need to go for a fourth-party audit?" The remark came as he flagged reports of poor quality in public projects during interactions with central secretaries and chief secretaries of states. Modi noted that while third-party auditing of works is routine practice, it may not be delivering the results expected of it. Presiding over the monthly Pragati review on Tuesday, the Prime Minister is understood to have described such lapses as "unacceptable", saying the system could not function this way. The session covered six projects in the railway, road and power sectors spread across nine states, together valued at more than Rs 30,000 crore. Modi said such projects should be tracked as a single integrated whole instead of being assessed as separate stretches, sections or packages. The Prime Minister's Office said in a statement, "PM said that speed of execution must be accompanied by uncompromising quality. He called upon ministries, states and implementing agencies to adopt modern technologies and strengthen quality assurance and supervision at every stage." While going through a power sector project, Modi is learnt to have remarked that raising generation alone serves little purpose unless matching transmission capacity is created, comparing the gap to "building dams without laying canals". Taking up cyber fraud, including cases of digital arrest, he said the focus must shift to prevention through training, awareness and education. He pressed for sustained and targeted campaigns aimed at senior citizens, young people and other vulnerable groups so they recognise common fraud methods, warning signals and safe online practices. He also sought regular skill upgrades for officials handling such cases. Home Secretary Govind Mohan presented details of measures taken by 20 states. national_raw_news.title: Seychelles seeks fisheries, aquaculture MoU with India to deepen blue economy cooperation
national_raw_news.content: Seychelles seeks fisheries, aquaculture MoU with India to deepen blue economy cooperation Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Seychelles seeks fisheries, aquaculture MoU with India to deepen blue economy cooperation ANI | Updated: Aug 26, 2026 13:21 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], August 26 (ANI): Seychelles has expressed interest in accelerating a bilateral Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with India focused exclusively on fisheries and aquaculture, as the two countries explore wider cooperation in marine research, technology and the blue economy, the Ministry of Fisheries , Animal Husbandry and Dairying said in a release. The proposal emerged during a high-level bilateral meeting held on August 25 between officials from India and Seychelles , where both sides discussed an advanced work plan and institutional mechanisms to turn existing cooperation into concrete projects. The Seychelles delegation, led by Minister of Fisheries , Agriculture and Blue Economy Wallace Cosgrow, and the India n delegation, led by Department of Fisheries Secretary Abhilaksh Likhi, reviewed existing frameworks and explored new areas of cooperation. The discussions covered marine aquaculture, modern hatcheries, tuna fisheries, fish stock assessment, post-harvest technology and marine conservation. The two sides also identified opportunities for knowledge transfer through technical studies, fisheries extension services and institutional training programmes. Digital technology emerged as another area of potential cooperation, with both sides discussing fisheries data systems and monitoring, control and surveillance infrastructure. They also explored the use of artificial intelligence in harvest management, along with opportunities to improve tuna processing, product diversification and sustainable fish waste management. The two countries agreed on the need for a structured annual work plan, regulatory alignment, faster commercialisation of joint scientific research, reciprocal laboratory access and jointly designed pilot projects to support long-term cooperation. The ministry said both sides viewed fisheries and the wider blue economy as important for economic growth, rural employment, sustainable development and food and nutritional security in the India n Ocean Region. India shared its recent achievements in the sector, including national fish production of 19.7 million tonnes and seafood exports worth USD 8.46 billion. It also highlighted initiatives focused on sustainable fisheries management, responsible harvesting and technology-driven infrastructure. Looking ahead, both sides emphasised mutual exposure visits, specialised technical exchanges and greater use of national Centres of Excellence to strengthen institutional capacity and share best practices. The meeting concluded with a shared focus on developing result-oriented action plans aimed at strengthening long-term maritime cooperation between India and Seychelles . According to official data from the National Bureau of Statistics, Seychelles ' imports from India stood at USD 91.73 million in 2024, while exports to India were USD 2.46 million. The data showed that trade between the two countries continued to have significant scope for expansion. national_raw_news.content: India’s 28 Regional Rural Banks Clock Highest-Ever Rs 10,176 Crore Profit In FY26 As Business Tops Rs 13.5 Lakh Crore Economy India’s 28 Regional Rural Banks Clock Highest-Ever Rs 10,176 Crore Profit In FY26 As Business Tops Rs 13.5 Lakh Crore Swarajya Staff Aug 26, 2026 | Updated 10:22 AM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer RRBs review meeting (Pic Via Finance Ministry/PIB) India's Regional Rural Banks have recorded their highest-ever consolidated net profit of Rs 10,176 crore in financial year 2025-26, marking a substantial 49 per cent increase from Rs 6,820 crore in the previous year. The total business of all 28 RRBs crossed Rs 13.5 lakh crore, surpassing the business levels of several individual public sector banks. The financial performance was reviewed during a comprehensive meeting held in New Delhi under the chairmanship of the Secretary, Department of Financial Services, attended by the chairman of NABARD, chairpersons of all 28 RRBs, and senior representatives from the Reserve Bank of India, SIDBI, sponsor banks, and the Department of Financial Services. Asset quality showed steady progress, with gross non-performing assets and net non-performing assets declining to historic lows of 5.3 per cent and 2.1 per cent, respectively. The 28 RRBs operate through a network of 22,273 branches across 26 states and three union territories, catering to approximately 700 districts nationwide. The institutions also recorded an increasing trend in their credit-deposit ratio, which climbed to an all-time high of 75.2 per cent during the financial year. RRBs achieved all prescribed targets and sub-targets under Priority Sector Lending, maintaining their focus on underserved and marginalised segments. The banks expanded rural financial inclusion by opening more than 54.98 lakh new Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana accounts during FY 2025-26. The Secretary of the Department of Financial Services appreciated the commendable performance and called upon all RRBs to sustain the momentum and further improve their performance so that the benefits of formal banking and government-sponsored schemes reach the last mile. He emphasised that RRBs must accelerate the adoption of modern banking technology and digital delivery of financial services to improve operational efficiency. national_raw_news.content: National Traders' Welfare Board holds 100th virtual meeting to strengthen government-trader dialogue, address grievances Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर National Traders' Welfare Board holds 100th virtual meeting to strengthen government-trader dialogue, address grievances ANI | Updated: Aug 26, 2026 05:31 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], August 26 (ANI): The National Traders' Welfare Board (NTWB) on Tuesday convened its 100th Virtual Conference (VC) Interaction Meeting, marking a milestone in its efforts to strengthen regular engagement between the government and the trader community across the country. According to the Ministry of Commerce & Industry press release, the meeting was chaired by NTWB Chairman Sunil J. Singhi. The Ministry of Commerce & Industry said the 100th VC Interaction Meeting reflects the importance of sustained and institutionalised engagement with the trader community, The decision to establish a dedicated virtual platform for retail traders was taken during the second meeting of the Board on February 7, 2024, chaired by Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal. During the meeting, it was proposed that a dedicated virtual platform be created to facilitate regular interaction with retail traders, disseminate information about government schemes and policies, and provide traders with an accessible mechanism to raise grievances and suggestions. The initiative was formally launched during the third meeting of the Board on July 11, 2024. Since then, VC Interaction Meetings have been conducted every Monday from 3 pm to 4 pm, providing a structured platform for continuous engagement with traders. According to the Ministry, the weekly platform has facilitated interaction with retail traders, dissemination of information on government schemes and policy initiatives, and submission of grievances and suggestions. The platform has also enabled the identification of recurring issues and their communication to the concerned ministries and departments for consideration and redressal. The platform has provided thousands of traders an avenue to directly share their concerns, suggestions and experiences with the government. It has connected small, medium and large traders from across the country on a common forum. Going forward, the initiative will focus on expanding participation, strengthening feedback and recommendation mechanisms, and facilitating more tangible outcomes from issues raised through the platform. The Ministry said traders play an important role in the Indian economy by linking producers with consumers, contributing to employment generation, sustaining local markets and supporting livelihoods across the country. The welfare and empowerment of traders, it added, have a direct bearing on employment, household incomes, local economies and the overall economic strength of the country.
